metadata.question: Did the Central Valley of California have a higher water height equivalent in October 2022 than March 2023?

data.raw_code: I'll analyze GRACE/GRACE-FO terrestrial water storage data to compare water height equivalent between October 2022 and March 2023 in California's Central Valley. 1. Search strategy: Use NASA GRACE/GRACE-FO data (terrestrial water storage anomaly) for water height equivalent. 2. Masking strategy: No cloud masking needed for GRACE data. 3. Logic: Compare mean water storage anomaly values between two months. Important considerations: - GRACE data is monthly, so I'll filter for specific months - Use 'lwe_thickness' band (equivalent water thickness in cm) - Check for data availability in both periods ```python import ee ee.Initialize(project='earthsense-436113') # 1. Define Central Valley geometry central_valley = ee.Geometry.Polygon([[ [-122.5, 40.5], [-121.0, 40.5], [-119.0, 36.5], [-121.0, 36.0], [-122.5, 36.0] ]]) # 2. Get GRACE data for two time periods # GRACE/GRACE-FO Mascon data (2002-present) grace_collection = ee.ImageCollection("NASA/GRACE/MASS_GRANDS/MASCON_CRI") # October 2022 (full month) oct_2022 = grace_collection.filterDate('2022-10-01', '2022-10-31') oct_count = oct_2022.size().getInfo() print(f"Oct 2022 Images: {oct_count}") # March 2023 (full month) mar_2023 = grace_collection.filterDate('2023-03-01', '2023-03-31') mar_count = mar_2023.size().getInfo() print(f"Mar 2023 Images: {mar_count}") # 3. Check for empty collections if oct_count == 0 or mar_count == 0: # Try alternative GRACE dataset if primary fails grace_alt = ee.ImageCollection("NASA/GRACE/MASS_GRIDS/LAND") oct_2022 = grace_alt.filterDate('2022-10-01', '2022-10-31') mar_2023 = grace_alt.filterDate('2023-03-01', '2023-03-31') oct_count = oct_2022.size().getInfo() mar_count = mar_2023.size().getInfo() print(f"Alt Oct 2022: {oct_count}, Alt Mar 2023: {mar_count}") if oct_count == 0 or mar_count == 0: print("C1") # 4. Process if data exists if oct_count > 0 and mar_count > 0: # Get mean images for each period oct_img = oct_2022.mean().select('lwe_thickness') mar_img = mar_2023.mean().select('lwe_thickness') # Get pixel counts and mean values oct_stats = oct_img.reduceRegion( reducer=ee.Reducer.mean().combine(ee.Reducer.count(), '', True), geometry=central_valley, scale=50000, maxPixels=1e9 ).getInfo() mar_stats = mar_img.reduceRegion( reducer=ee.Reducer.mean().combine(ee.Reducer.count(), '', True), geometry=central_valley, scale=50000, maxPixels=1e9 ).getInfo() # Extract values oct_mean = oct_stats.get('lwe_thickness_mean') oct_pixels = oct_stats.get('lwe_thickness_count') mar_mean = mar_stats.get('lwe_thickness_mean') mar_pixels = mar_stats.get('lwe_thickness_count') print(f"Oct 2022: {oct_mean:.2f} cm, Pixels: {int(oct_pixels)}") print(f"Mar 2023: {mar_mean:.2f} cm, Pixels: {int(mar_pixels)}") # 5. Validate and determine answer if oct_mean is None or mar_mean is None: print("C3") elif oct_pixels == 0 or mar_pixels == 0: print("C2") else: # Check for invalid values (GRACE anomaly typically -50 to +50 cm) if abs(oct_mean) > 200 or abs(mar_mean) > 200: print("C3") elif oct_mean > mar_mean: print("A") else: print("B") ```

import ee
ee.Initialize(project='earthsense-436113')

# 1. Define Central Valley geometry
central_valley = ee.Geometry.Polygon([[
    [-122.5, 40.5],
    [-121.0, 40.5],
    [-119.0, 36.5],
    [-121.0, 36.0],
    [-122.5, 36.0]
]])

# 2. Get GRACE data for two time periods
# GRACE/GRACE-FO Mascon data (2002-present)
grace_collection = ee.ImageCollection("NASA/GRACE/MASS_GRANDS/MASCON_CRI")

# October 2022 (full month)
oct_2022 = grace_collection.filterDate('2022-10-01', '2022-10-31')
oct_count = oct_2022.size().getInfo()
print(f"Oct 2022 Images: {oct_count}")

# March 2023 (full month)
mar_2023 = grace_collection.filterDate('2023-03-01', '2023-03-31')
mar_count = mar_2023.size().getInfo()
print(f"Mar 2023 Images: {mar_count}")

# 3. Check for empty collections
if oct_count == 0 or mar_count == 0:
    # Try alternative GRACE dataset if primary fails
    grace_alt = ee.ImageCollection("NASA/GRACE/MASS_GRIDS/LAND")
    oct_2022 = grace_alt.filterDate('2022-10-01', '2022-10-31')
    mar_2023 = grace_alt.filterDate('2023-03-01', '2023-03-31')
    
    oct_count = oct_2022.size().getInfo()
    mar_count = mar_2023.size().getInfo()
    
    print(f"Alt Oct 2022: {oct_count}, Alt Mar 2023: {mar_count}")
    
    if oct_count == 0 or mar_count == 0:
        print("<answer>C1</answer>")

# 4. Process if data exists
if oct_count > 0 and mar_count > 0:
    # Get mean images for each period
    oct_img = oct_2022.mean().select('lwe_thickness')
    mar_img = mar_2023.mean().select('lwe_thickness')
    
    # Get pixel counts and mean values
    oct_stats = oct_img.reduceRegion(
        reducer=ee.Reducer.mean().combine(ee.Reducer.count(), '', True),
        geometry=central_valley,
        scale=50000,
        maxPixels=1e9
    ).getInfo()
    
    mar_stats = mar_img.reduceRegion(
        reducer=ee.Reducer.mean().combine(ee.Reducer.count(), '', True),
        geometry=central_valley,
        scale=50000,
        maxPixels=1e9
    ).getInfo()
    
    # Extract values
    oct_mean = oct_stats.get('lwe_thickness_mean')
    oct_pixels = oct_stats.get('lwe_thickness_count')
    mar_mean = mar_stats.get('lwe_thickness_mean')
    mar_pixels = mar_stats.get('lwe_thickness_count')
    
    print(f"Oct 2022: {oct_mean:.2f} cm, Pixels: {int(oct_pixels)}")
    print(f"Mar 2023: {mar_mean:.2f} cm, Pixels: {int(mar_pixels)}")
    
    # 5. Validate and determine answer
    if oct_mean is None or mar_mean is None:
        print("<answer>C3</answer>")
    elif oct_pixels == 0 or mar_pixels == 0:
        print("<answer>C2</answer>")
    else:
        # Check for invalid values (GRACE anomaly typically -50 to +50 cm)
        if abs(oct_mean) > 200 or abs(mar_mean) > 200:
            print("<answer>C3</answer>")
        elif oct_mean > mar_mean:
            print("<answer>A</answer>")
        else:
            print("<answer>B</answer>")
